column2: Remaining turned away from a work can be told apart from being partway through turning back toward it, though the two may look alike at a given moment.
What is wrong in a first wrongful act can be distinguished from the sin of remaining turned away from it afterward.
An agent can remain turned away from a work while the knowledge of it stays present to them.
A work has a character, such as being a wrong or a good, that one can acknowledge or fail to acknowledge apart from acknowledging that one did it.
Acknowledging a wrong of one's own for what it is, without any deed, does not exclude remaining turned away from it.
There is something one can do in deed toward a past work of one's own, even when the work itself cannot be undone.
Where nothing can be repaired, facing a work in deed can consist in bearing its consequences willingly as one's own, as distinct from merely submitting to them.
Attention can perceive a work's character accurately without acknowledging the work as one's own.
Attention to a work, however close, can be held while no deed toward it is done.
Repentance can arrive at a facing in deed as well as in acknowledgment.
Where some deed toward the work is possible, contrition that never issues in any deed falls short of the facing that is sin's contrary.
